exercises.q: Отец авансом дал мне деньги за ___ (неделя, acc. sg.).
exercises.prompt: Father advanced me a week's allowance.
exercises.why: **неделя → неделю** (acc. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -я — declines like DLI's тётя: A. тётю. Ending -я → -ю.  Declension: sg. неделя · недели · неделе · неделю · неделей · неделе; pl. недели · недель · неделям · недели · неделями · неделях.  «The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.prompt: He has been working all day long.
exercises.why: **день → день** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in -ь — declines like DLI's автомобиль: A. автомобиль. Ending -ь → -ь.  **весь → весь** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with день). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новый: A. anim. = G., inan. = N.. Ending — (no ending) → — (no ending).  Declension: sg. день · дня · дню · день · днём · дне; pl. дни · дней · дням · дни · днями · днях.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Все испытанное им за ___ (последний месяц, acc. sg.) утвердило его отношение к жизни, к людям.
exercises.why: **месяц → месяц** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a hard consonant — declines like DLI's дом: A. дом. exercises.q: В ___ (свободный вечер, acc. pl.) Евгений Петрович имел обыкновение рассказывать Сереже сказки.
exercises.why: **вечер → вечера** (acc. pl.). Masculine, inanimate; nominative plural вечера; declines like DLI's слова (hard stem): A. слова. Ending — (no ending) → -а.  **свободный → свободные** (acc. pl., agreeing with вечера). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новые: A. anim. = G., inan. = N.. Ending -ые → -ые.  Declension: sg. вечер · вечера · вечеру · вечер · вечером · вечере; pl. вечера · вечеров · вечерам · вечера · вечерами · вечерах.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48. exercises.q: А их нельзя разве читать в ___ (другой день, acc. pl.)?
exercises.why: **день → дни** (acc. pl.). Masculine, inanimate; nominative plural дни; declines like DLI's словари (soft stem): A. словари. Ending -ь → -и, with the fleeting -е- of the stem dropped: дн- + -и.  **другой → другие** (acc. pl., agreeing with дни). Adjective type III, guttural (after г, к, х) — declines like DLI's русские: A. anim. = G., inan. = N.. Ending -ие → -ие.  Declension: sg. день · дня · дню · день · днём · дне; pl. дни · дней · дням · дни · днями · днях.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending -ой if stressed: новый — молодой; русский — плохой, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension.» «The adjective «большой» belongs to the guttural type, in spite of its -ш-: большого, большому, большим, о большом.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: А если она и не добра, так притвориться может на ___ (твой час, acc. sg.).
exercises.why: **час → час** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a hard consonant — declines like DLI's дом: A. дом. Ending — (no ending) → — (no ending).  **твой → твой** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with час). A possessive — declines like DLI's мой / наш. Ending -й → -й.  Declension: sg. час · часа · часу · час · часом · часе; pl. часы · часов · часам · часы · часами · часах.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «Notice the similarity of the endings of the possessives to the form of «они».» мой · моё — моего — моему — моим — о моём; моя — моей — мою; мои — моих — моим — моими — о моих. — DLI, Lessons 47–48.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).
